Formulation  
A 28-year-old woman with no prior headache history presents with an acute, severe left-sided headache. Family history of migraines is present. No clear precipitating psychosocial stressors identified. Denies systemic or neurological symptoms. Mild functional impact on work performance noted. Early intervention with analgesia and monitoring recommended. No mental health diagnosis or risk concerns evident at this time.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Acute severe headache of uncertain etiology  
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve headache relief and return to normal functioning  
- Clinical Goal(s): Manage headache symptoms, monitor for red flag signs requiring further investigation  
- Actions (Patient): Take prescribed analgesics regularly with food, maintain hydration and rest, monitor symptoms for deterioration or new symptoms  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe appropriate analgesics (paracetamol and stronger pain relief advised), educate patient on warning signs, arrange follow-up if symptoms worsen or persist  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: analgesic use, hydration, rest, warning signs including worsening pain, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing headache severity, new neurological symptoms, fever, neck stiffness, rash, recurrent episodes  
- Coping Strategies: Rest, hydration, medication adherence
